title: Sanggenon C induces P53-mediated apoptotic cell death associated with modulation of the MDM2-P53 axis in non-small cell lung cancer cells.
authors: Chen, Yan; Xie, Nanlan; Chen, Yuanyuan; Ren, Ling; Zhu, Weimin; Huang, Yijiao; Shan, Yongfeng; Xiang, Pei
journal: Food and chemical toxicology : an international journal published for the British Industrial Biological Research Association
one_liner_zh: 该文研究天然化合物Sanggenon C通过MDM2-P53轴诱导肺癌细胞凋亡，虽含分子对接和MD模拟，但核心是药物-蛋白互作而非蛋白质-DNA互作，与TF-DNA课题关联较弱。
abstract: Non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) remains a major cause of cancer-related mortality and is characterized by disruption of P53-dependent cell death pathways. The present study investigated the effects of sanggenon C (SC), a natural polyphenolic compound, on cell death regulation focusing on the murine double minute 2 (MDM2)-P53 axis. SC was evaluated in NSCLC cell lines with different TP53 statuses and in xenograft and lung colonization models. SC preferentially induced apoptotic cell death in TP53 wild-type cells compared with TP53-mutant or TP53-null cells, accompanied by reduced clonogenic survival, migration, and invasion in P53-proficient cells, as well as decreased tumor burden and lung colonization in vivo in a TP53-dependent manner. Mechanistically, SC enhanced P53 protein stability by reducing ubiquitination and prolonging its half-life without altering TP53 mRNA expression, as demonstrated by cycloheximide chase and ubiquitination assays. DARTS-LC-MS/MS identified 72 candidate SC-associated proteins, and subsequent biochemical validation, including microscale thermophoresis and co-immunoprecipitation, implicated MDM2 as an SC-associated binding partner, further supported by molecular docking and molecular dynamics analyses. Consistently, SC decreased MDM2 protein abundance, while MDM2 overexpression partially attenuated SC-induced P53 stabilization. These findings indicate that SC induces P53-mediated apoptotic cell death in association with modulation of the MDM2-P53 axis.
abstract_zh: 非小细胞肺癌（NSCLC）仍是癌症相关死亡的主要原因，其特征为P53依赖性细胞死亡通路受损。本研究探讨了天然多酚类化合物桑根酮C（sanggenon C, SC）对细胞死亡调控的影响，重点关注鼠双微体2（murine double minute 2, MDM2）-P53轴。在具有不同TP53状态的NSCLC细胞系以及异种移植和肺定植模型中评估了SC的作用。与TP53突变或TP53缺失细胞相比，SC在TP53野生型细胞中优先诱导凋亡性细胞死亡，并伴随P53功能完整细胞中克隆形成存活、迁移和侵袭能力的降低，以及在体内以TP53依赖性方式减少肿瘤负荷和肺定植。机制上，SC通过减少泛素化并延长P53半衰期来增强P53蛋白稳定性，而不改变TP53 mRNA表达，这通过放线菌酮追踪和泛素化实验得到证实。DARTS-LC-MS/MS鉴定出72个候选SC相关蛋白，后续生化验证（包括微量热泳动和免疫共沉淀）提示MDM2为SC相关结合伙伴，分子对接和分子动力学分析进一步支持这一结果。一致地，SC降低MDM2蛋白丰度，而MDM2过表达部分减弱了SC诱导的P53稳定化。这些发现表明，SC通过与MDM2-P53轴的调控相关联，诱导P53介导的凋亡性细胞死亡。
